title: S1 V3.9 — Macro composite, 30-minute timing, temporal stability, and full fail-pattern report
question: Do the Macro composite verdict and each 30-minute entry slot justify S1 advisory score adjustments under the current V3.9 trade export, and what does the full section 5 fail-pattern/BB/DXY/MTF breakdown show for the same trades? Revision 4 adds: is V3.9's backtest edge stable across time, or concentrated in an earlier stretch of the same export (added to test an overfitting concern about TradingView-developed strategies)?
hypothesis: Macro and 30-minute timing may change expectancy, but should not be assumed to be binary permissions without V3.9 evidence; any live adjustment must be small, integer, and always shown with its own sample size and confidence interval. The temporal-stability check does not retrain or re-tune the strategy; it only tests whether the already-fixed backtest's win rate/profit factor holds up in the most recent 30% of trades by entry time versus the earlier 70%.

findings.title: Macro WAIT remained profitable
findings.detail: 211 matched trades; WR 56.87%, PF 1.837. The evidence does not support a categorical S1 block; rank score is 0 (middle of the 3 verdicts), not negative.

findings.title: NEUTRAL is the weakest Macro verdict under the rank-score method
findings.detail: NEUTRAL has the lowest win rate (53.66%) of the three verdicts despite the highest PF (1.963) and the smallest sample (82) — it ranks last (rank_score -1), reversing its prior +1.4 shrinkage-based ranking. Both methods are reading the same 82 trades; they disagree because they rank on different statistics (win rate vs shrunk average return).

findings.title: Asia was not the weak V3.9 session
findings.detail: 154 trades; WR 57.79%, PF 1.999. The inherited Asia-only observation rule is not supported; asia ranks best of the 3 scored sessions (rank_score +1).

findings.title: Use the matching 30-minute slot
findings.detail: The operational score looks up the current HH:00/HH:30 entry slot's integer rank score (section 13.2), range -2...+2. 5 of 48 slots are low-sample (n<5) and score 0.

findings.title: normal_sl is the dominant fail type, not immediate_loss
findings.detail: 104 of 197 losses (52.8%) are a clean normal_sl stop-out; immediate_loss is 25.9% (51 trades). Descriptive context, not a live-impact mechanism.

findings.title: Counter-trend (4H bearish) entries underperform
findings.detail: 146 trades against a bearish 4H RSI state: WR 47.95% vs 60.2% for the 304 aligned trades. Descriptive context (section 5.1 item 8), not currently a live-impact mechanism.

findings.title: Chronological holdout: flagged stable, not clearly degraded
findings.detail: 70/30 holdout split by entry time: in-sample (2024-01-05 to 2025-11-18, n=315) WR 57.14% PF 1.886; held-out (2025-11-20 to 2026-07-10, n=135) WR 54.07% PF 1.832. Held-out win rate sits inside the in-sample 95% CI [51.62, 62.49] and held-out PF stays above 1.0, so the fixed rule (section 5.1 item 11) flags 'stable', not 'degraded'. This is a chronological-bucket check on one already-fixed backtest export, not a re-optimized walk-forward — see results.json method.temporal_stability_limitation before treating this as proof the strategy is not overfit.

findings.title: 2026Q2 was the weakest full quarter in the export, not 2026Q1
findings.detail: Quarterly win rate ranges 48.94%-62.96% across 11 quarters with no monotonic trend. 2026Q1 was the best quarter (n=55, WR 60.0%, PF 2.563); 2026Q2 was the weakest full quarter (n=47, WR 48.94%, PF 1.429), though still PF>1. The quarterly shape is worth cross-referencing against execution records before concluding the backtest edge itself changed: a live result that weakens while the backtest holds points at execution, not at the strategy.

card_summary: Macro composite and 30-minute timing were scored into S1 for months; neither survives review, and both were revoked.
